solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Arrange insurance and head for shelter (4,5)

blocks.note: to take out cover is to buy an insurance policy
to duck out of rain or gunfire into somewhere safe

annotation.surface: Someone sorts out a policy and then runs from the storm.
annotation.walkthrough: The two halves sound like a sequence of errands, but each is a complete meaning of the same phrase.
annotation.definitionFit: Taking cover means both buying insurance and sheltering from danger.

entries.clue: Sadly lost ring in workman’s gear (5)

indicatorNotes.Sadly: things done sadly are done badly, so the letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
a ring is round, like the letter O

annotation.surface: A workman mourns a wedding ring that has vanished somewhere in his kit.
annotation.walkthrough: The ring reads as jewellery; in wordplay a ring is almost always the letter O.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the gear a tradesman carries is the kit he works with.

entries.clue: Captures youngster and dozes (7)

blocks.note: a kid is a youngster
naps = dozes

annotation.surface: Someone grabs a child and then nods off, an oddly calm criminal.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole answer is spelt out in the clue: the thing seized plus the snooze that follows.
annotation.definitionFit: To kidnap someone is to capture them and hold them.

entries.clue: Protection from officer by end of day — and no mistake (9)

indicatorNotes.end of: the end of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: a cop is a police officer
last letter of DAY
what is right contains no mistake

annotation.surface: A policeman offers protection by nightfall, and he means it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Protection' looks like police business, which is why 'officer' sits beside it; the answer is legal protection for creative work.
annotation.definitionFit: Copyright protects authors and artists from having their work copied.

entries.clue: Portuguese explorer at first very assured skinning fish and lizard (5,2,4)

indicatorNotes.at first: take only the first letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: first letters of Very, Assured, Skinning
the cod, a fish
the agama, an Old World lizard

annotation.surface: An explorer confidently prepares a catch of fish and a lizard for the pot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Skinning' looks like an instruction to strip letters off 'fish', but it only lends its S. The agama is a crossword regular among lizards.
annotation.definitionFit: Vasco da Gama was the Portuguese navigator who first sailed from Europe to India.

entries.clue: Found in cage in tribunal (3)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer sits in the next word

blocks.note: the letters sit just after the T, inside the word

annotation.surface: Something discovered in a prisoner's cell during a trial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cage' suggests a prison, but it is the ribcage; the definition is a description, not a synonym.
annotation.definitionFit: Ribs are the bones that make up the ribcage.

entries.clue: European’s address from individuals backing Republican (5)

indicatorNotes.backing: going backwards: the word is read right to left

blocks.note: individuals = ones
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

annotation.surface: A political speech given by a European, with people rallying behind a Republican.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Address' means a form of address, not a speech or a street: Señor is Spanish for Mr or sir.
annotation.definitionFit: Señor is how a Spanish man is addressed, the equivalent of Mr.

entries.clue: Notes first of rays coming from the sun (5)

indicatorNotes.first of: take the first letter of the next word

blocks.note: SO and LA, two notes of the sol-fa scale
first letter of RAYS

annotation.surface: Someone jots down notes on the first sunbeams of the day.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Notes' suggests writing, but here it is two musical notes from do-re-mi.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym from the Latin sol, sun, as in solar power or the solar wind.

entries.clue: Rain spoilt outside broadcast, one at African capital (7)

indicatorNotes.spoilt: what is spoilt is ruined, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: RAIN rearranged
OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast
I is the Roman numeral one

annotation.surface: Bad weather ruins a television crew's location shoot in an African capital.
annotation.walkthrough: An outside broadcast is a TV or radio programme made away from the studio, so OB reads naturally in a story about rain.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the capital of Kenya is one African capital among many.

entries.clue: They haven’t won, but have a drink with athlete (7-2)

blocks.note: a runner is an athlete
to sup is to drink

annotation.surface: Losing competitors console themselves with a drink alongside an athlete.
annotation.walkthrough: 'With' only places the two pieces side by side, so the athlete can come first though the clue names the drink first.
annotation.definitionFit: A description: those who finish second, or lower, in a contest are by definition not the winners.

entries.clue: Dictionary (American) includes one page on tragic figure (7)

indicatorNotes.includes: the outer pieces hold the next piece inside them

blocks.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
I = one, P = page
US = American

annotation.surface: An American dictionary gives a single page to a figure from Greek tragedy.
annotation.walkthrough: The brackets make 'American' look like a description of the dictionary, but it is its own piece, and the dictionary and the nationality together wrap round 'one page'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the king of Sophocles' play, who unknowingly kills his father and marries his mother, is the classic tragic hero.

entries.clue: Gold signs overlap (7)

indicatorNotes.overlap: the two words share the letter where they meet, so one copy of L is dropped

blocks.note: the Bull (Taurus), a sign of the zodiac; its final L is shared
the Lion (Leo), another sign

annotation.surface: Stock-market indicators for gold run into one another.
annotation.walkthrough: One word, 'signs', supplies two zodiac signs, and 'overlap' tells you BULL and LION share their L.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: the word means precious metal in bulk bars, and gold is the usual example.

entries.clue: Steps look sound (5)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Stair' can mean a whole flight of steps, so the plural clue word fits

indicatorNotes.sound: say the word and listen to it

blocks.note: to stare is to look hard

annotation.surface: An instruction to check that some steps are safe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look sound' reads as 'seem solid'; instead 'sound' tells you to say a word for 'look' out loud.
annotation.definitionFit: A stair, or a flight of stairs, is a set of steps.

entries.clue: Beating snooper up intentionally (2,7)

indicatorNotes.Beating: a beating knocks things about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Someone beat up a spy, and they meant to do it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Up' looks like part of the phrase 'beating up', but it is fodder too.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an adverbial phrase meaning deliberately, with intent.

entries.clue: In trouble, prophesy about church’s response (11)

blocks.note: to predict is to prophesy
the congregation's reply to a prayer

annotation.surface: A prophet foresees how a church will respond to trouble.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In trouble' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'trouble'. PREDIC-AMEN-T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a tight spot or awkward situation is trouble.

entries.clue: Had been noticed, on return (3)

annotation.definitionNote: 'Was' and 'had been' are close past forms of 'be', not an exact swap

indicatorNotes.on return: going back: the word is read right to left

blocks.note: saw = noticed

annotation.surface: Someone had been spotted on their way back.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue looks like a report from a lookout; 'on return' is the instruction to turn SAW around.
annotation.definitionFit: Was and had been are both past forms of the verb to be.

entries.clue: Who is Fred? Badly desired! (6,3)

indicatorNotes.Badly: the letters are put together badly, out of order

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: Nobody knows who Fred is, yet he is badly wanted.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark tries to split the clue into two sentences; 'Badly desired' reads as 'wanted very much', but 'Badly' belongs to the anagram.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are past participles for something longed for.

entries.clue: Prague first ordered citrus foods (11)

indicatorNotes.ordered: put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: In Prague, a diner orders the fruit course first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ordered' reads as a restaurant order, which suits the food.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the large sour breakfast fruit is one of the citrus family.

entries.clue: Ian Fleming character reviewed Blake Bros. (4,5)

indicatorNotes.reviewed: viewed again in a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A critic reviews a firm called Blake Brothers for a Bond book.
annotation.walkthrough: Rosa Klebb is the SMERSH villain with the poisoned shoe blade in From Russia with Love.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: one of many characters in the James Bond novels.

entries.clue: Strange Tuscan sign for churches? (11)

indicatorNotes.Strange: the letters of the next word are made strange, rearranged

blocks.note: TUSCAN rearranged
Aries, the Ram, a sign of the zodiac

annotation.surface: An odd Tuscan signpost points the way to churches.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that churches are only one example of sanctuaries.
annotation.definitionFit: Churches traditionally offered sanctuary, so each is a sanctuary.

entries.clue: Streamlined housing getting energy from sodium battery first (7)

indicatorNotes.first: the pieces before it go at the front

blocks.note: Na is the chemical symbol for sodium
a cell is a battery
E is the symbol for energy

annotation.surface: A sleek new house draws its power from a sodium battery above all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Housing' suggests homes, but a nacelle houses an engine. 'First' puts NA CELL ahead of the E.
annotation.definitionFit: A nacelle is the streamlined casing around an aircraft engine.

entries.clue: Sleep in khaki pyjamas (3)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer is inside the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of the first word run into the first letter of the second

annotation.surface: Someone sleeps in army-coloured nightwear.
annotation.walkthrough: Kip is informal British for a sleep or nap.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: informal British slang for a sleep or nap.

entries.clue: Cocky type, 22, was almost captured (4-3)

indicatorNotes.almost: the word is almost complete, its last letter dropped
indicatorNotes.captured: the second piece has been captured inside the first

blocks.note: the answer to 22 across
WAS without its last letter

annotation.surface: A cocky type was nearly caught.
annotation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to KNOLL; KNO(WA)LL.
annotation.definitionFit: A know-all is a cocky person who thinks they know everything.

entries.clue: Woman cuddling baby, eating a hot snack (9)

indicatorNotes.cuddling: a cuddle wraps arms round someone, so the woman goes round the baby
indicatorNotes.eating: what is eaten goes inside, so the baby holds A

blocks.note: Ena, a woman's name
a baby is a child
A as printed

annotation.surface: A woman holds her baby while eating a hot snack.
annotation.walkthrough: Two containers nest, innermost first: the baby eats 'a', and the woman then cuddles the result. Ena is a stock crossword woman's name.
annotation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a tortilla filled and baked in a hot chilli sauce.

entries.clue: Peaceful girl, alluring one, topless, at end of promenade (5)

indicatorNotes.topless: remove the top, the first letter
indicatorNotes.at end of: take the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: SIREN, an alluring woman, without its first letter
last letter of PROMENADE

annotation.surface: An alluring girl sunbathes topless at the end of the seafront.
annotation.walkthrough: Irene is from the Greek for peace, which is why she is a 'peaceful girl'. A promenade is a British seafront walkway.
annotation.definitionFit: The name Irene means peace in Greek.

entries.clue: Hillock seen returning from hill on Kerrera (5)

indicatorNotes.seen: the answer can be seen inside the words
indicatorNotes.returning: going back: read right to left

blocks.note: hi-LL ON K-errera, read backwards

annotation.surface: A little mound spotted on the way back from a hill on a Scottish island.
annotation.walkthrough: Kerrera is a small island off Oban in western Scotland; its name matters only for its K.
annotation.definitionFit: A knoll is a small rounded hill, a hillock.

entries.clue: Sports car for such idle eaters (5)

blocks.note: a British make of sports car, founded by Colin Chapman
in the Odyssey, an island people who ate a fruit and forgot all wish to go home

annotation.surface: A fast car wasted on people who only sit about eating.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Such idle eaters' asks which word goes before 'eaters': the lotus-eaters, who forgot home after eating the fruit.
annotation.definitionFit: One sense is a brand name for a car; the other is the flower whose fruit Homer's idle eaters lived on.

entries.clue: Those lumberjack chaps! (7)

blocks.note: the surface reads this as pointing at some lumberjacks; the setter means people who cut down trees
the surface reads this as a cheery 'those guys!'; the setter means an informal word for men

annotation.surface: An admiring exclamation about some lumberjacks.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer means both tree-fellers and chaps, so the lumberjacks are fellers twice over.
annotation.definitionFit: Lumberjacks fell trees, and fellers is a colloquial word for men.

entries.clue: I am Caesar’s dim follower. Problem? (3)

blocks.note: 'I am' translated into Latin, Caesar's language
the word that follows 'dim' in the name of the Chinese dumpling meal
an arithmetic exercise set in school

annotation.surface: Caesar confesses to being a slow-witted hanger-on and asks if that is a problem.
annotation.walkthrough: Three definitions in a row: Latin, a Chinese dish, and a schoolroom problem. The question mark marks a sum as only one kind of problem.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a schoolroom calculation is one kind of problem, hence the question mark.

entries.clue: Graceful and neat, oddly concealing limb (7)

indicatorNotes.oddly: arranged oddly, so the letters are rearranged
indicatorNotes.concealing: the rearranged letters hide the next word inside them

blocks.note: NEAT rearranged
a leg is a limb

annotation.surface: A graceful, tidy figure is oddly hiding one arm or leg.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts you to take odd letters, but here it rearranges NEAT, which then wraps round LEG: E-LEG-ANT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: stylish and pleasing in movement or appearance.

entries.clue: Bird will change course back by far end of lake (5)

indicatorNotes.back: the course is changed back, so the word runs in the opposite direction, right to left
indicatorNotes.far end of: take the last letter of the next word

blocks.note: to veer is to change course
last letter of LAKE

annotation.surface: A bird swerves back over the far side of a lake.
annotation.walkthrough: A reeve is the female ruff, a wading bird; the name is rare outside crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: The reeve is the female of the ruff, a sandpiper.

entries.clue: Postpones work on the two arcades, according to Spooner (9)

indicatorNotes.according to Spooner: swap the opening sounds of the two words, as Rev. Spooner did

blocks.note: both = the two; it takes the M from the other word
shopping malls = arcades; it takes the B in exchange

annotation.surface: A developer shelves building work on two shopping arcades.
annotation.walkthrough: To mothball a project is to put it into storage for later, like clothes packed with mothballs.
annotation.definitionFit: To mothball something is to put work on it on hold.
